title: The Goat and the Goatherd

full_text:
A goatherd was driving his flock home to the fold at sundown when a stubborn goat strayed from the trail, browsing on sweet thyme upon a steep rocky outcrop. The goatherd whistled and called, but the goat refused to heed his voice.

Losing his temper, the goatherd picked up a jagged stone and hurled it at the animal, intending merely to frighten her back to the path. But the stone struck the goat's horn squarely, snapping it off near the skull with a sickening crack.

Terrified of what his master would say when he saw the mutilated prize animal, the goatherd fell upon his knees, stroked the goat's brow, and begged: "I implore you, dear goat, do not tell the master that I broke your horn!"

The bleeding goat turned her amber eyes upon the trembling man and replied with dry irony:

"You foolish man! Even if I were to keep my mouth tightly closed, my broken horn would shout your deed to all the world! How can you conceal a fault that is written plainly upon my brow for all to see?"
moral: No plea of silence can hide a misdeed that speaks for itself in plain sight.
